subject: Kickoff: ISV interop playground for LangChain & LlamaIndex integrations
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@crescendo.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: ISV interop playground proposal

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Crescendo’s use of multimodal retrieval + prompt tuning is a great fit for a small, hands-on interop project we’ve been meaning to run. I’m proposing we stand up a short "interop playground" to validate:

- SDK integration patterns for LangChain and LlamaIndex with Redwood’s hosted and dedicated runtimes
- Trace propagation across SDK hooks so observability works end-to-end (LangChain traces -> Redwood traces)
- Prompt-tooling compatibility (prompt templates, function/tool-calling) and a simple eval sweep to check fidelity

What we’re asking for from Crescendo: a sandbox dataset (or a synthetic subset), an engineer who can join the kickoff and weekly syncs (preferably someone familiar with your Retriever stack), and a staging API key/ingress point. On our side we’ll provide a small SOW, sample repos, and a prebuilt demo (not production) that exercises the three areas above.

Suggested timeline (flexible):
- Nov 30: 60-min kickoff (technical + PM)
- Week of Dec 6: 2-day PoC work (pairing sessions)
- Week of Dec 13: short evaluation + learnings doc, optional next-steps (pilot/SOW)

I attached a short proposal and a kickoff agenda stub. Can you confirm the right technical contact and whether Nov 30 morning (PST) works for you?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: crescendo-interp-playground-proposal.pdf

From: Ellen Park <ellen@crescendo.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Rivera <diego@crescendo.ai>, partner-success@crescendo.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ISV interop playground proposal

Hi Vanessa —

Love the structure here. Diego is our lead on retrieval infra and can cover the LangChain/LlamaIndex clients. He’s copied. Nov 30 PST morning works for us; Diego can take the kickoff and we’ll pull PM representation if needed.

Quick notes from our side:
- We can expose a synthetic subset of our corpus in a secured S3 bucket and create temporary credentials for the PoC.
- We’ll need a short SOW that clarifies data handling and retention during the PoC (we can route through our security team).
- Diego: will you confirm which runtimes you want as targets (hosted/dedicated/private)?

Happy to take the proposal and agenda — thanks for putting this together.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Partners | Crescendo Labs
ellen@crescendo.ai

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for looping me in. A couple of internal asks before kickoff:

1) Engineering leads: I’ll put Jonas and I on client-side integration and trace hooking. Ben, can you confirm whether we demo hosted runtime + a lightweight dedicated config (4xA10-like) or include the private on-prem path? My recommendation: hosted + dedicated for the PoC — private deploys add operational overhead and aren’t necessary for initial validation.

2) Quick checklist for Diego (we should send this before kickoff):
   - Expected QPS for the demo queries
   - Sample schema for retriever payloads (fields + vector dim)
   - Any rate-limited endpoints or gated resources

3) Security: we need the SOW template and the minimal set of logs we’ll retain for debugging. I’ll draft an MNDA-lite if Crescendo prefers.

I put a stub agenda in drive and attached to the external invite after Vanessa confirms time.

—Marissa
